summary: Returns the value as a presentation, or throws.
description: An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard looks for the methods that define the type — `getId`, `getSlides`. A stub that implements them passes, which is what makes code using this guard testable outside the runtime.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a presentation.

throws.InvalidPresentationException: the value is not a presentation.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
const presentation = SlidesApp.getActivePresentation();

requirePresentation(presentation); // => presentation
requirePresentation({}); // throws InvalidPresentationException
requirePresentation(null); // throws InvalidPresentationException
```
